text:
objective: To examine decadal Land Use Land Cover (LULC) changes from 1990–2020 and simulate LULC for 2030 and 2050 under different scenarios for Taiwan, incorporating demographic factors.
country: Taiwan
land_use_classes: Barren; Uncultivated; Shallow water; Deep water; Built-up; Forest; Cultivated
baseline_years: 1990; 2000; 2010; 2020
target_future_years: 2030; 2050
scenarios: 2-variables (Elevation, Distance to roads); 3-variables (Elevation, Distance to roads, Distance to rivers); 5-variables (Aspect, elevation, hillshade, Distance to rivers, slope); 6-variables (Aspect, elevation, hillshade, Distance to rivers, Distance to roads, slope)
analysis_methods: Maximum likelihood classifier (supervised classification) for LULC classification; Support Vector Machine led Markov-chain method for LULC simulation; Accuracy assessment using confusion matrix, Overall Accuracy, Kappa coefficient, Producer's Accuracy, User's Accuracy, Root-Mean-Square-Error (RMSE)
simulation_method_advantages: The integration of Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification with Markov-chain modeling enables precise LULC classification and dynamic land-cover predictions; SVM provides higher classification accuracy than ANN & maximum-likelihood classifiers; The hybrid approach leverages both precise classification of LULC classes and probabilistic future predictions, improving accuracy in complex urban landscapes.
predictors: Aspect; Elevation; Hillshade; Distance to river; Distance to road; Slope
population_selected: Yes
data_sources: Landsat series satellite images (Landsat 5, 7, 8 Surface Reflectance Tier 1); SRTM-Digital Elevation Model (30 m) for aspect, elevation, hillshade, slope; Open Street Maps & Google Earth for roads; Google Earth Engine for satellite image collection and processing
tools_software_used: Google Earth Engine; GIS software (not explicitly named)
validation_performed: Yes
validation_methods: Confusion matrix method using ground control points (GCPs); Calculation of Overall Accuracy, Kappa coefficient, Producer's Accuracy, User's Accuracy
validation_data_sources: 655 ground control points (GCPs) as reference for historical LULC validation; 300 GCPs for predicted LULC 2020 validation
key_findings: Built-up area increased by 140% from 1990 to 2020; Under the 6-variables scenario, built-up area is simulated to increase by 223% from 1990 by 2050; Barren area decreased by 49.17% from 1990 to 2020; Water Deep area decreased by nearly 49% from 1990 to 2020; Forest area expanded by 2.19% from 1990 to 2020; Cultivated lands increased by 15.27% from 1990 to 2020; The 3-variables scenario (Elevation, Distance to roads, Distance to rivers) is considered the best for simulation, providing results almost identical to the 6-variables scenario with fewer variables; The simulated LULC for 2020 validation recorded an overall accuracy of 0.87 and kappa index of 0.74.
implications: The combination of Taiwan’s negative population growth rate and the simultaneous increase in impervious surfaces creates a significant topic for discussion; Findings provide crucial information for decision and policy makers regarding expected urban expansion direction and public infrastructure needs; Supports development of sustainable land-use strategies and understanding of urbanization's ecological impact.
limitations: Satellite images before 1990 were not considered due to high cloud coverage; The Markov model assumes transition probabilities remain constant over time (stationarity), which may not hold in areas experiencing rapid shifts; Transition probabilities are static, which can overlook non-linear dynamics of LULC change; Model assumes each cell’s transition probability is independent of its neighbors, potentially overlooking spatial dependencies.
future_directions: Not specified
scalability: The national-scale approach is essential for countries with diverse land uses and complex socio-ecological contexts, offering a model for future studies in similar regions; The methodology is applicable to other rapidly urbanizing, mid-sized economies facing land-use and environmental challenges.
novelty: First study to conduct LULC classification and simulation (1990–2050) for the complete Taiwan territory; Incorporates Taiwan’s demographic shifts, such as negative population growth, in modeling future LULC; One of the first to apply the integrated SVM-Markov approach at a national scale for Taiwan; A long-term, large-scale spatio-temporal study considering demographic factors as no previous study has done for Taiwan.
